slides.heading: The Epidemiological Triad
slides.subtitle: Disease results from the interaction of agent, host, and environment.

terms.definition: Influences exposure, susceptibility or response — may be the patient, carrier, suspect or contact.
All external conditions (physical, biological, socio-economic) that allow host exposure.
Ability of an organism to cause disease / damage the host.
Ability to infect and multiply within the host.
Number of organisms / amount of toxin needed to induce disease.

slides.heading: Stages of Disease
rows: From initial infection to first appearance of signs/symptoms.
Overt signs & symptoms; peak/acme; pathognomonic (specific) sign appears.
Onset of complications leading to death.

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: Rabies = very high pathogenicity/virulence but low infectivity.
